title: Digital signatures
syllabusUnit: Unit IV: Digital Signature Standards & Verification
covers: Signing & verifying, DSS/DSA, RSA signatures, non-repudiation
learningGoals: You will be able to explain how digital signatures provide authenticity and non-repudiation.
You will be able to trace the Sign(Hash, PrivateKey) and Verify(Hash, Signature, PublicKey) workflow.
You will be able to contrast RSA signatures with the Digital Signature Standard (DSS/DSA).

lessonCards.title: The Digital Wax Seal
lessonCards.analogy: A physical handwritten signature can be forged with tracing paper, but a mathematical signature cannot be forged without the private key.
lessonCards.coreConcept: A digital signature binds an identity to a specific message: Signer hashes the document and encrypts the hash with their private key. Anyone with the public key can verify.
lessonCards.example: Guarantees three things: Message Integrity, Sender Authentication, and Non-repudiation.

lessonCards.title: The Sign & Verify Dance
lessonCards.analogy: Locking the seal with your private stamp; the entire world uses your public viewer to check the seal matches.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Signing: S = Sign(H(M), PrivateKey). Verification: Compute H(M), decrypt signature with PublicKey, and check if both hash digests match exactly.
lessonCards.example: If even a single comma in M is altered, H(M) completely changes and verification fails instantly.

lessonCards.title: DSA & ECDSA: The Signature Standard
lessonCards.analogy: A protocol designed specifically to sign fast without being used for general encryption.
lessonCards.coreConcept: NIST Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) operates over discrete logs; Elliptic Curve DSA (ECDSA) operates over elliptic curves.
lessonCards.example: Crucial rule: the random nonce k used during signing must NEVER be reused or leaked (Sony PS3 hack).

questions.prompt: What key is used to CREATE a digital signature, and what key is used to VERIFY it?
options: Created with the sender's Private Key; verified with the sender's Public Key
Created with Public Key; verified with Private Key
Created with AES key; verified with password
Created with Wi-Fi password; verified with router
questions.explanation: Only the private key owner can create the valid mathematical signature, but anyone possessing their public key can confirm its validity.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Private key signs; public key verifies.
Reversing keys is encryption, not digital signing.
AES is symmetric and cannot provide non-repudiation.
Wi-Fi passwords are unrelated.
questions.realWorldExample: Software operating system updates are signed by developer private keys to verify legitimacy.

questions.prompt: Why is the message HASHED before being signed, rather than signing the raw document directly?
options: Hashing produces a small fixed-size digest (e.g. 256 bits), making signature computation fast and preventing algebraic attacks
Because documents cannot be read by computers
Signing hashes makes files invisible
To delete old versions of the file
questions.explanation: Public key mathematics is slow; hashing megabyte-sized contracts down to 32 bytes enables sub-millisecond signing.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Hashing provides speed, efficiency, and security against existential forgery.
Computers process raw documents easily.
Signatures do not hide document text.
Version control is an application feature.
questions.realWorldExample: RSA-PSS (Probabilistic Signature Scheme) hashes messages with salt before signing.

questions.prompt: What disastrous security failure caused the Sony PlayStation 3 ECDSA signature key to be completely compromised in 2010?
options: Sony used a static constant number instead of a fresh random nonce k for every signature
The PS3 ran out of storage space
A hacker guessed the password 'password'
Sony used 512-bit RSA
questions.explanation: In ECDSA, signing two distinct messages with the same nonce k allows an attacker to solve simple linear equations and extract the private signing key!
wrongExplanations: Correct! Nonce reuse in ECDSA immediately leaks the master private key.
Storage space does not compromise private keys.
ECDSA private keys are huge 256-bit numbers, not dictionary words.
Sony used ECDSA, not RSA.
questions.realWorldExample: Fail0verflow extracted Sony's master root key because Sony's developers set nonce k = 4 (a constant).

questions.prompt: What critical legal and technical property do digital signatures provide that symmetric MACs CANNOT?
options: Non-Repudiation (proof to a third-party judge that only the private key holder could have signed)
Data compression
Faster download speeds
Virus detection
questions.explanation: Since symmetric MACs share the same secret key between sender and receiver, either party could have generated the tag. Digital signatures prove origin to any neutral third party.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Non-repudiation ensures the sender cannot falsely deny signing.
Signatures slightly increase file size, not compress.
Network speeds depend on bandwidth.
Signatures verify origin, not malware absence.
questions.realWorldExample: Under the US ESIGN Act and EU eIDAS regulation, cryptographic digital signatures have full legal standing.

questions.prompt: In RSA signature verification, if the decrypted signature value does not match the computed hash of the received message, what does it mean?
options: The message was modified in transit OR the signature was forged
The server clock is fast
The user needs to restart Windows
The signature has expired
questions.explanation: A signature mismatch proves mathematically that either the message bits were altered, or the signature was created by a different private key.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Either data tampering or fraudulent sender identity occurred.
Clock drift does not change mathematical hash equality.
OS restarts do not fix corrupted cryptographic hashes.
Signature expiration is checked via certificate timestamps.
questions.realWorldExample: Package managers like apt and pacman reject update packages if signature verification fails.

options: A modern high-speed Edwards-curve digital signature algorithm (EdDSA) that resists side-channel attacks
An old DES cipher mode
A hash algorithm from 1980
A router protocol
questions.explanation: Designed by Daniel J. Bernstein, Ed25519 uses Curve25519 to provide fast, constant-time signatures resilient to cache-timing attacks and nonce failures.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Ed25519 is the modern standard for SSH keys, Git commits, and blockchain nodes.
DES is obsolete symmetric encryption.
SHA is hashing.
BGP is a routing protocol.
questions.realWorldExample: GitHub and OpenSSH recommend Ed25519 keys as the modern default over legacy RSA.

ashRecap: A digital signature is your unbreakable personal stamp. You sign with your secret Private Key, and the whole world verifies it with your Public Key!
